title: A slice of the sky
caption: A panorama of the Very Large Telescope under a moonlit sky, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This panoramic photograph, spanning approximately 230 degrees, takes in ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT) and a broad slice of sky. The four large Unit Telescopes dominate the foreground, and nearby sit the four round enclosures of the 1.8-metre Auxiliary Telescopes, one on the left and three on the right. On the left, what looks like a rippling ocean is actually the cloud layer below the mountaintop.

Cerro Paranal is so high, at 2600 metres, that those clouds lie beneath it; the Pacific Ocean really is in that direction, hidden under them. Above the clouds glows the Moon, lighting both the telescopes and the sky, and just above it a bright point that looks like a star is the planet Jupiter.

Other familiar sights are scattered across the sky. The tight group of stars near the top middle is the Pleiades, or Seven Sisters. Capella shines above the second Unit Telescope from the left, while Pollux and Castor, the heads of Gemini, appear above and slightly right of the rightmost one.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based panoramic photograph by Gerhard Hüdepohl covering about 230 degrees; the packet does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: No eye takes in a 230-degree sweep at once, and the camera also records the moonlit scene with more light than an observer would perceive.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Above the shadowed Auxiliary Telescope on the right sits the open cluster Praesepe, also called the Beehive Cluster, with the bright star Procyon above it near the top of the frame. The Unit Telescopes' mirrors, 8.2 metres across, let astronomers see things four billion times fainter than the eye can. ESO Photo Ambassador Gerhard Hüdepohl took the panorama.
alt: A wide panorama of four large telescope enclosures and smaller round domes on a mountaintop, with a sea of clouds and a bright Moon at left under a starry sky.
